original_question: Can one construct the moduli space Delta_G of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk as an inductive limit of finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly identifies the object Δ_G, the moduli problem of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk, and the precise structural question of whether this moduli space can be realized as an inductive limit of finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks.
missing_details: The paper’s standing convention is that the base field k is algebraically closed unless otherwise specified.
G should be stated to be a finite group.
To make the question stand-alone, the punctured formal disk should be identified as Spec k((t)).
Because G-torsors have nontrivial automorphisms, the intended moduli object is really a stack-valued moduli space, not an honest scheme.
The open case is the general finite-group case; the paper notes that the case where G is a semidirect product of a p-group and a tame cyclic group is already known.
It helps to say explicitly that the desired inductive system is one of Deligne-Mumford stacks of finite type over k.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field, let G be a finite group, and let Δ_G denote the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk Spec k((t)). Since G-torsors have nontrivial automorphisms, can the corresponding moduli functor be represented by a stack, more precisely by an ind-Deligne-Mumford stack over k, i.e. an inductive limit of Deligne-Mumford stacks of finite type over k, in the general finite-group case?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 8 rather than any statement in the introduction: Problem 8.1 asks almost verbatim whether one can construct the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk as an inductive limit of finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks. Section 2.3 is where the paper introduces Δ_G as the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk in the wild McKay correspondence, and the paper’s convention section supplies the ambient assumption that the base field is algebraically closed unless stated otherwise. The paragraph immediately after Problem 8.1 adds the hidden stand-alone details that the relevant fine moduli object should be a stack because G-torsors have nontrivial automorphisms, and that the already-settled case is when G is a semidirect product of a p-group and a tame cyclic group, so the open problem is the general finite-group case.
